title: Binary Search in 1 Minute | DSA Short
summary: Binary search in under a minute: how to find a number between 1 and 1000 in ten guesses, step by step, plus the two mistakes almost everyone makes.
author: Vinay Mishra
original_value: Explains binary search with a number-guessing game, walks low, mid and high across a real array, and shows two real Python mistakes (unsorted input and / versus //).
sources: Standard binary search algorithm (any algorithms textbook)
Python language reference: integer division (//) versus true division (/)

scenes.headline: 1 to 1000. Ten guesses.
scenes.narration: Think of any number from one to a thousand. I will find it in ten guesses. Here is how.

scenes.headline: The trick
items: Too big? Drop the right half
Too small? Drop the left half
scenes.narration: The list must be sorted. Check the middle. If it is too big, throw away the right half. Too small, throw away the left half.

scenes.headline: Find 23
scenes.narration: Say we want twenty-three. The middle is sixteen, too small, so go right. Now fifty-six, too big, so go left. Twenty-three. Found in three steps.

scenes.headline: Two classic mistakes
scenes.narration: Two mistakes. Running it on an unsorted list gives wrong answers. And in Python, use double slash for the middle, or you get a decimal.

scenes.headline: That is it
scenes.narration: Every step halves the search. A thousand items take ten guesses. A million take twenty. Follow for the next interview question.
